bw.2011.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $AB$ and $CD$ be two diameters of the circle $\mathcal{C}$. For an arbitrary point $P$ on $\mathcal{C}$, let $R$ and $S$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $P$ to $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. Show that the length of $RS$ is independent of the choice of $P$.

bw.2011.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $P$ be a point inside a square $ABCD$ such that $PA:PB:PC$ is $1:2:3$. Determine the angle $\angle BPA$.

bw.2011.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $E$ be an interior point of the convex quadrilateral $ABCD$. Construct triangles $ABF$, $BCG$, $CDH$ and $DAI$ on the outside of the quadrilateral such that the similarities $\triangle ABF\sim\triangle DCE$, $\triangle BCG\sim\triangle ADE$, $\triangle CDH\sim\triangle BAE$ and $\triangle DAI\sim\triangle CBE$ hold. Let $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ be the projections of $E$ on the lines $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$, respectively. Prove that if the quadrilateral $PQRS$ is cyclic, then $$EF\cdot CD=EG\cdot DA=EH\cdot AB=EI\cdot BC.$$

bw.2011.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.14.reviewed_statement: The incircle of a triangle $ABC$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$, respectively. Let $G$ be a point on the incircle such that $FG$ is a diameter. The lines $EG$ and $FD$ intersect at $H$. Prove that $CH\parallel AB$.

bw.2011.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.15.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that $\angle ADB=\angle BDC$. Suppose that a point $E$ on the side $AD$ satisfies the equality $$AE\cdot ED+BE^2=CD\cdot AE.$$ Show that $\angle EBA=\angle DCB$.

bw.2011.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ be any integer. Define the sequence $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ by $x_0=a$, $x_1=3$, and for all $n>1$ $$x_n=2x_{n-1}-4x_{n-2}+3.$$ Determine the largest integer $k_a$ for which there exists a prime $p$ such that $p^{k_a}$ divides $x_{2011}-1$.

bw.2011.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.17.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $d$ such that whenever $d$ divides a positive integer $n$, $d$ will also divide any integer obtained by rearranging the digits of $n$.

bw.2011.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.18.reviewed_statement: Determine all pairs $(p,q)$ of primes for which both $p^2+q^3$ and $q^2+p^3$ are perfect squares.

bw.2011.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $p\neq 3$ be a prime number. Show that there is a non-constant arithmetic sequence of positive integers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_p$ such that the product of the terms of the sequence is a cube.

bw.2011.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.20.reviewed_statement: An integer $n\geq 1$ is called balanced if it has an even number of distinct prime divisors. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that there are exactly two balanced numbers among $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$ and $n+3$.

bw.2012.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.1.reviewed_statement:
The numbers from $1$ to $360$ are partitioned into $9$ subsets of consecutive integers and the sums of the numbers in each subset are arranged in the cells of a $3\times 3$ square. Is it possible that the square turns out to be a magic square?
Remark: A magic square is a square in which the sums of the numbers in each row, in each column and in both diagonals are all equal.

bw.2012.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be real numbers. Prove that $$ab+bc+ca+\max\{|a-b|, |b-c|, |c-a|\}\leq 1+\frac13(a+b+c)^2.$$

bw.2012.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.3.reviewed_statement:
(a) Show that the equation $$\lfloor x\rfloor(x^2+1)=x^3,$$ where $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the largest integer not larger than $x$, has exactly one real solution in each interval between consecutive positive integers.
(b) Show that none of the positive real solutions of this equation is rational.

bw.2012.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that for infinitely many pairs $(a,b)$ of integers the equation $$x^{2012}=ax+b$$ has among its solutions two distinct real numbers whose product is $1$.

bw.2012.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ for which $$f(x+y)=f(x-y)+f\big(f(1-xy)\big)$$ holds for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

bw.2012.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.6.reviewed_statement: There are $2012$ lamps arranged on a table. Two persons play the following game. In each move the player flips the switch of one lamp, but he must never get back an arrangement of the lit lamps that has already been on the table. A player who cannot move loses. Which player has a winning strategy?

bw.2012.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.7.reviewed_statement: On a $2012\times 2012$ board, some cells on the top-right to bottom-left diagonal are marked. None of the marked cells is in a corner. Integers are written in each cell of this board in the following way. All the numbers in the cells along the upper and the left sides of the board are $1$'s. All the numbers in the marked cells are $0$'s. Each of the other cells contains a number that is equal to the sum of its upper neighbour and its left neighbour. Prove that the number in the bottom right corner is not divisible by $2011$.

bw.2012.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.8.reviewed_statement: A directed graph does not contain directed cycles. The number of edges in any directed path does not exceed $99$. Prove that it is possible to colour the edges of the graph in $2$ colours so that the number of edges in any single-coloured directed path in the graph will not exceed $9$.

bw.2012.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.9.reviewed_statement: Zeroes are written in all cells of a $5\times 5$ board. We can take an arbitrary cell and increase by $1$ the number in this cell and all cells having a common side with it. Is it possible to obtain the number $2012$ in all cells simultaneously?

bw.2012.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.10.reviewed_statement:
Two players $A$ and $B$ play the following game. Before the game starts, $A$ chooses $1000$ not necessarily different odd primes, and then $B$ chooses half of them and writes them on a blackboard. In each turn a player chooses a positive integer $n$, erases some primes $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$ from the blackboard and writes all the prime factors of $p_1p_2\cdots p_n-2$ instead (if a prime occurs several times in the prime factorization of $p_1p_2\cdots p_n-2$, it is written as many times as it occurs). Player $A$ starts, and the player whose move leaves the blackboard empty loses the game. Prove that one of the two players has a winning strategy and determine who.
Remark: Since $1$ has no prime factors, erasing a single $3$ is a legal move.

bw.2012.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle A=60^\circ$. The point $T$ lies inside the triangle in such a way that $\angle ATB=\angle BTC=\angle CTA=120^\circ$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Prove that $TA+TB+TC=2AM$.

bw.2012.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $P_0, P_1, \ldots, P_8=P_0$ be successive points on a circle and $Q$ be a point inside the polygon $P_0P_1\cdots P_7$ such that $\angle P_{i-1}QP_i=45^\circ$ for $i=1, \ldots, 8$. Prove that the sum $$\sum_{i=1}^{8}P_{i-1}P_i^2$$ is minimal if and only if $Q$ is the centre of the circle.

bw.2012.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $H$ be its orthocentre. Denote by $H_A$, $H_B$ and $H_C$ the second intersection of the circumcircle with the altitudes from $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Prove that the area of triangle $H_AH_BH_C$ does not exceed the area of triangle $ABC$.

bw.2012.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.14.reviewed_statement: Given a triangle $ABC$, let its incircle touch the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$, respectively. Let $G$ be the midpoint of the segment $DE$. Prove that $\angle EFC=\angle GFD$.

bw.2012.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.15.reviewed_statement: The circumcentre $O$ of a given cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ lies inside the quadrilateral but not on the diagonal $AC$. The diagonals of the quadrilateral intersect at $I$. The circumcircle of the triangle $AOI$ meets the sides $AD$ and $AB$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively; the circumcircle of the triangle $COI$ meets the sides $CB$ and $CD$ at points $R$ and $S$, respectively. Prove that $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.

bw.2012.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $n$, $m$ and $k$ be positive integers satisfying $(n-1)n(n+1)=m^k$. Prove that $k=1$.

bw.2012.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $n$. Find all triples $(n,k,p)$, where $n$ and $k$ are positive integers and $p$ is a prime number, such that $$n^{d(n)}-1=p^k.$$

bw.2012.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.18.reviewed_statement: Find all triples $(a,b,c)$ of integers satisfying $a^2+b^2+c^2=20122012$.

bw.2012.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.19.reviewed_statement: Show that $n^n+(n+1)^{n+1}$ is composite for infinitely many positive integers $n$.

bw.2012.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.20.reviewed_statement: Find all integer solutions of the equation $2x^6+y^7=11$.

bw.2013.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Assume that $n$ numbers are to be chosen from the table $$\begin{array}{cccc}0 & 1 & \cdots & n-1\\ n & n+1 & \cdots & 2n-1\\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ (n-1)n & (n-1)n+1 & \cdots & n^2-1\end{array}$$ with no two of them from the same row or the same column. Find the maximal value of the product of these $n$ numbers.

bw.2013.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k, y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n$ be distinct integers. A polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients satisfies $$P(x_1)=P(x_2)=\cdots=P(x_k)=54,$$ $$P(y_1)=P(y_2)=\cdots=P(y_n)=2013.$$ Determine the maximal value of $kn$.

bw.2013.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of real numbers. Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f\big(xf(y)+y\big)+f\big(-f(x)\big)=f\big(yf(x)-y\big)+y$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

bw.2013.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that the following inequality holds for all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$: $$\frac{x^3}{y^2+z^2}+\frac{y^3}{z^2+x^2}+\frac{z^3}{x^2+y^2}\geq\frac{x+y+z}{2}.$$

bw.2013.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.5.reviewed_statement: Numbers $0$ and $2013$ are written at two opposite vertices of a cube. Some real numbers are to be written at the remaining $6$ vertices of the cube. On each edge of the cube the difference between the numbers at its endpoints is written. When is the sum of squares of the numbers written on the edges minimal?

bw.2013.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.6.reviewed_statement: Santa Claus has at least $n$ gifts for $n$ children. For $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, the $i$-th child considers $x_i>0$ of these items to be desirable. Assume that $$\frac{1}{x_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{x_n}\leq 1.$$ Prove that Santa Claus can give each child a gift that this child likes.

bw.2013.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.7.reviewed_statement: A positive integer is written on a blackboard. Players $A$ and $B$ play the following game: in each move one has to choose a proper divisor $m$ of the number $n$ written on the blackboard ($1<m<n$) and replace $n$ with $n-m$. Player $A$ makes the first move, then players move alternately. The player who can't make a move loses the game. For which starting numbers is there a winning strategy for player $B$?

bw.2013.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.8.reviewed_statement: There are $n$ rooms in a sauna, each has unlimited capacity. No room may be attended by a female and a male simultaneously. Moreover, males want to share a room only with males that they don't know and females want to share a room only with females that they know. Find the biggest number $k$ such that any $k$ couples can visit the sauna at the same time, given that two males know each other if and only if their wives know each other.

bw.2013.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.9.reviewed_statement: In a country there are $2014$ airports, no three of them lying on a line. Two airports are connected by a direct flight if and only if the line passing through them divides the country in two parts, each with $1006$ airports in it. Show that there are no two airports such that one can travel from the first to the second, visiting each of the $2014$ airports exactly once.

bw.2013.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.10.reviewed_statement: A white equilateral triangle is split into $n^2$ equal smaller triangles by lines that are parallel to the sides of the triangle. Denote a line of triangles to be all triangles that are placed between two adjacent parallel lines that form the grid. In particular, a triangle in a corner is also considered to be a line of triangles. We are to paint all triangles black by a sequence of operations of the following kind: choose a line of triangles that contains at least one white triangle and paint this line black. Find the smallest and largest possible number of operations.

bw.2013.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.11.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AC>AB$, let $D$ be the projection of $A$ on $BC$, and let $E$ and $F$ be the projections of $D$ on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $G$ be the intersection point of the lines $AD$ and $EF$. Let $H$ be the second intersection point of the line $AD$ and the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Prove that $AG\cdot AH=AD^2$.

bw.2013.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.12.reviewed_statement: A trapezoid $ABCD$ with bases $AB$ and $CD$ is such that the circumcircle of the triangle $BCD$ intersects the line $AD$ in a point $E$, distinct from $A$ and $D$. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle $ABE$ is tangent to the line $BC$.

bw.2013.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.13.reviewed_statement: All faces of a tetrahedron are right-angled triangles. It is known that three of its edges have the same length $s$. Find the volume of the tetrahedron.

bw.2013.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.14.reviewed_statement: Circles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of the same radius intersect in two points, one of which is $P$. Denote by $A$ and $B$, respectively, the points diametrically opposite to $P$ on each of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. A third circle of the same radius passes through $P$ and intersects $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in the points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Show that the line $XY$ is parallel to the line $AB$.

bw.2013.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.15.reviewed_statement: Four circles in a plane have a common centre. Their radii form a strictly increasing arithmetic progression. Prove that there is no square with each vertex lying on a different circle.

bw.2013.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.16.reviewed_statement: We call a positive integer $n$ delightful if there exists an integer $k$, $1<k<n$, such that $$1+2+\cdots+(k-1)=(k+1)+(k+2)+\cdots+n.$$ Does there exist a delightful number $N$ satisfying the inequalities $$2013^{2013}<\frac{N}{2013^{2013}}<2013^{2013}+4\ ?$$

bw.2013.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $c$ and $n>c$ be positive integers. Mary's teacher writes $n$ positive integers on a blackboard. Is it true that for all $n$ and $c$ Mary can always label the numbers written by the teacher by $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ in such an order that the cyclic product $(a_1-a_2)(a_2-a_3)\cdots(a_{n-1}-a_n)(a_n-a_1)$ would be congruent to either $0$ or $c$ modulo $n$?

bw.2013.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.18.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs $(x,y)$ of integers such that $y^3-1=x^4+x^2$.

bw.2013.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0$ be a positive integer and $a_n=5a_{n-1}+4$ for all $n\geq 1$. Can $a_0$ be chosen so that $a_{54}$ is a multiple of $2013$?

bw.2013.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.20.reviewed_statement: Find all polynomials $f$ with non-negative integer coefficients such that for all primes $p$ and positive integers $n$ there exist a prime $q$ and a positive integer $m$ such that $f(p^n)=q^m$.

bw.2014.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2014.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_N$ be real numbers satisfying $a_0=a_N=0$ and $$a_{i+1}-2a_i+a_{i-1}=a_i^2\quad\text{for } i=1, 2, \ldots, N-1.$$ Prove that $a_i\leq 0$ for $i=1, 2, \ldots, N-1$.

bw.2014.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.3.reviewed_statement: Positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy $\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c=3$. Prove the inequality $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^3+b}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{b^3+c}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{c^3+a}}\leq\frac{3}{\sqrt2}.$$

bw.2014.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.4.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f$ defined on all real numbers and taking real values such that $$f\big(f(y)\big)+f(x-y)=f\big(xf(y)-x\big)$$ for all real numbers $x$, $y$.

bw.2014.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.5.reviewed_statement: Given positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ that satisfy the equalities $$a^2+d^2-ad=b^2+c^2+bc\quad\text{and}\quad a^2+b^2=c^2+d^2,$$ find all possible values of the expression $\frac{ab+cd}{ad+bc}$.

bw.2014.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.6.reviewed_statement: In how many ways can we paint $16$ seats in a row, each red or green, in such a way that the number of consecutive seats painted in the same colour is always odd?

bw.2014.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.7.reviewed_statement: Let $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{30}$ be a permutation of the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, 30$. For how many permutations does the equality $$\sum_{k=1}^{30}|p_k-k|=450$$ hold?

bw.2014.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2014.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.9.reviewed_statement: What is the least possible number of cells that can be marked on an $n\times n$ board such that for each $m>\frac{n}{2}$ both diagonals of any $m\times m$ sub-board contain a marked cell?

bw.2014.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.10.reviewed_statement: In a country there are $100$ airports. Super-Air operates direct flights between some pairs of airports (in both directions). The traffic of an airport is the number of airports it has a direct Super-Air connection with. A new company, Concur-Air, establishes a direct flight between two airports if and only if the sum of their traffics is at least $100$. It turns out that there exists a round-trip of Concur-Air flights that lands in every airport exactly once. Show that then there also exists a round-trip of Super-Air flights that lands in every airport exactly once.

bw.2014.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$. The perpendicular to $AB$ from $C$ meets $AB$ at $D$ and $\Gamma$ again at $E$. The bisector of angle $C$ meets $AB$ at $F$ and $\Gamma$ again at $G$. The line $GD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $H$ and the line $HF$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $I$. Prove that $AI=EB$.

bw.2014.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.12.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ is given. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the segment $AB$ and $T$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$. The point $K$ inside the triangle $ABC$ is such that $MATK$ is an isosceles trapezoid with $AT\parallel MK$. Show that $AK=KC$.

bw.2014.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a square inscribed in a circle $\omega$ and let $P$ be a point on the shorter arc $AB$ of $\omega$. Let $CP\cap BD=R$ and $DP\cap AC=S$. Show that triangles $ARB$ and $DSR$ have equal areas.

bw.2014.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.14.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that the line $BD$ bisects the angle $ABC$. The circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ intersects the sides $AD$ and $CD$ in the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. The line through $D$ and parallel to $AC$ intersects the lines $BC$ and $BA$ at the points $R$ and $S$, respectively. Prove that the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ lie on a common circle.

bw.2014.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.15.reviewed_statement: The sum of the angles $A$ and $C$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is less than $180^\circ$. Prove that $$AB\cdot CD+AD\cdot BC<AC(AB+AD).$$

bw.2014.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.16.reviewed_statement: Determine whether $712!+1$ is a prime number.

bw.2014.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.17.reviewed_statement: Do there exist pairwise distinct rational numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ such that $$\frac{1}{(x-y)^2}+\frac{1}{(y-z)^2}+\frac{1}{(z-x)^2}=2014?$$

bw.2014.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $n$ be a positive integer. Find the number of quadruples $(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)$ with $a_i\in\{0, 1, \ldots, p^n-1\}$ for $i=1, 2, 3, 4$, such that $$p^n\mid(a_1a_2+a_3a_4+1).$$

bw.2014.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $m$ and $n$ be relatively prime positive integers. Determine all possible values of $$\gcd\left(2^m-2^n,\ 2^{m^2+mn+n^2}-1\right).$$

bw.2014.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.20.reviewed_statement: Consider a sequence of positive integers $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ such that for $k\geq 2$ we have $$a_{k+1}=\frac{a_k+a_{k-1}}{2015^i},$$ where $2015^i$ is the maximal power of $2015$ that divides $a_k+a_{k-1}$. Prove that if this sequence is periodic then its period is divisible by $3$.

bw.2015.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.1.reviewed_statement: For $n\geq 2$, an equilateral triangle is divided into $n^2$ congruent smaller equilateral triangles. Determine all ways in which real numbers can be assigned to the $\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{2}$ vertices so that three such numbers sum to zero whenever the three vertices form a triangle with edges parallel to the sides of the big triangle.

bw.2015.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ be real numbers satisfying $0\leq a_i\leq 1$ for $i=1, \ldots, n$. Prove the inequality $$(1-a_1^n)(1-a_2^n)\cdots(1-a_n^n)\leq(1-a_1a_2\cdots a_n)^n.$$

bw.2015.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n>1$ be an integer. Find all non-constant real polynomials $P(x)$ satisfying, for any real $x$, the identity $$P(x)P(x^2)P(x^3)\cdots P(x^n)=P\left(x^{\frac{n(n+1)}{2}}\right).$$

bw.2015.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.4.reviewed_statement: A family wears clothes of three colours: red, blue and green, with a separate, identical laundry bin for each colour. At the beginning of the first week, all bins are empty. Each week, the family generates a total of $10$ kg of laundry (the proportion of each colour is subject to variation). The laundry is sorted by colour and placed in the bins. Next, the heaviest bin (only one of them, if there are several that are heaviest) is emptied and its contents washed. What is the minimal possible storing capacity required of the laundry bins in order for them never to overflow?

bw.2015.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying the equation $$|x|f(y)+yf(x)=f(xy)+f(x^2)+f\big(f(y)\big)$$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

bw.2015.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.6.reviewed_statement: Two players play the following game. At the outset there are two piles, containing $10000$ and $20000$ tokens, respectively. A move consists of removing any positive number of tokens from a single pile or removing $x>0$ tokens from one pile and $y>0$ tokens from the other, where $x+y$ is divisible by $2015$. The player who cannot make a move loses. Which player has a winning strategy?

bw.2015.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.7.reviewed_statement: There are $100$ members in a ladies' club. Each lady has had tea (in private) with exactly $56$ of her lady friends. The Board, consisting of the $50$ most distinguished ladies, have all had tea with one another. Prove that the entire club may be split into two groups in such a way that, within each group, any lady has had tea with any other.

bw.2015.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.8.reviewed_statement: With inspiration drawn from the rectilinear network of streets in New York, the Manhattan distance between two points $(a,b)$ and $(c,d)$ in the plane is defined to be $$|a-c|+|b-d|.$$ Suppose only two distinct Manhattan distances occur between all pairs of distinct points of some point set. What is the maximal number of points in such a set?

bw.2015.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.9.reviewed_statement: Let $n>2$ be an integer. A deck contains $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ cards, numbered $1, 2, 3, \ldots, \frac{n(n-1)}{2}$. Two cards form a magic pair if their numbers are consecutive, or if their numbers are $1$ and $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$. For which $n$ is it possible to distribute the cards into $n$ stacks in such a manner that, among the cards in any two stacks, there is exactly one magic pair?

bw.2015.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.10.reviewed_statement:
A subset $S$ of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ is called balanced if for every $a$ from $S$ there exists some $b$ from $S$, $b\neq a$, such that $\frac{a+b}{2}$ is in $S$ as well.
(a) Let $k>1$ be an integer and let $n=2^k$. Show that every subset $S$ of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ with $|S|>\frac{3n}{4}$ is balanced.
(b) Does there exist an $n=2^k$, with $k>1$ an integer, for which every subset $S$ of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ with $|S|>\frac{2n}{3}$ is balanced?

bw.2015.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.11.reviewed_statement: The diagonals of parallelogram $ABCD$ intersect at $E$. The bisectors of $\angle DAE$ and $\angle EBC$ intersect at $F$. Assume $ECFD$ is a parallelogram. Determine the ratio $AB:AD$.

bw.2015.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.12.reviewed_statement: A circle passes through vertex $B$ of the triangle $ABC$, intersects its sides $AB$ and $BC$ at points $K$ and $L$, respectively, and touches the side $AC$ at its midpoint $M$. The point $N$ on the arc $BL$ (which does not contain $K$) is such that $\angle LKN=\angle ACB$. Find $\angle BAC$ given that the triangle $CKN$ is equilateral.

bw.2015.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $B$ in the triangle $ABC$, where $AB=1$. The incentre of triangle $BCD$ coincides with the centroid of triangle $ABC$. Find the lengths of $AC$ and $BC$.

bw.2015.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.14.reviewed_statement: In the non-isosceles triangle $ABC$ an altitude from $A$ meets side $BC$ in $D$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and let $N$ be the reflection of $M$ in $D$. The circumcircle of triangle $AMN$ intersects the side $AB$ in $P\neq A$ and the side $AC$ in $Q\neq A$. Prove that $AN$, $BQ$ and $CP$ are concurrent.

bw.2015.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.15.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, the interior and exterior angle bisectors of $\angle BAC$ intersect the line $BC$ in $D$ and $E$, respectively. Let $F$ be the second point of intersection of the line $AD$ with the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$. Let $O$ be the circumcentre of the triangle $ABC$ and let $D'$ be the reflection of $D$ in $O$. Prove that $\angle D'FE=90^\circ$.

bw.2015.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.16.reviewed_statement: Denote by $P(n)$ the greatest prime divisor of $n$. Find all integers $n\geq 2$ for which $$P(n)+\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor=P(n+1)+\lfloor\sqrt{n+1}\rfloor.$$

bw.2015.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.17.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which $n^{n-1}-1$ is divisible by $2^{2015}$, but not by $2^{2016}$.

bw.2015.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $f(x)=x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0$ be a polynomial of degree $n\geq 1$ with $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integer roots. Assume that there exist distinct primes $p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_{n-1}$ such that $a_i>1$ is a power of $p_i$, for all $i=0, 1, \ldots, n-1$. Find all possible values of $n$.

bw.2015.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.19.reviewed_statement: Three pairwise distinct positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$, with $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$, satisfy $$a\mid(b-c)^2,\quad b\mid(a-c)^2,\quad c\mid(a-b)^2.$$ Prove that there does not exist a non-degenerate triangle with side lengths $a$, $b$, $c$.

bw.2015.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.20.reviewed_statement: For any integer $n\geq 2$, we define $A_n$ to be the number of positive integers $m$ with the following property: the distance from $n$ to the nearest multiple of $m$ is equal to the distance from $n^3$ to the nearest multiple of $m$. Find all integers $n\geq 2$ for which $A_n$ is odd. (Note: The distance between two integers $a$ and $b$ is defined as $|a-b|$.)

bw.2016.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.1.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of primes $(p,q)$ such that $$p^3-q^5=(p+q)^2.$$

bw.2016.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.2.reviewed_statement:
Prove or disprove the following hypotheses.
(a) For all $k\geq 2$, each sequence of $k$ consecutive positive integers contains a number that is not divisible by any prime number less than $k$.
(b) For all $k\geq 2$, each sequence of $k$ consecutive positive integers contains a number that is relatively prime to all other members of the sequence.

bw.2016.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.3.reviewed_statement: For which integers $n=1, \ldots, 6$ does the equation $$a^n+b^n=c^n+n$$ have a solution in integers?

bw.2016.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be integers such that $n\mid a+b+c+d$ and $n\mid a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2$. Show that $$n\mid a^4+b^4+c^4+d^4+4abcd.$$

bw.2016.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.5.reviewed_statement: Let $p>3$ be a prime such that $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$. Given a positive integer $a_0$ define the sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ of integers by $a_n=a_{n-1}^{2^n}$ for all $n=1, 2, \ldots$. Prove that it is possible to choose $a_0$ such that the subsequence $a_N, a_{N+1}, a_{N+2}, \ldots$ is not constant modulo $p$ for any positive integer $N$.

bw.2016.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.6.reviewed_statement: The set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 10\}$ is partitioned into three subsets $A$, $B$ and $C$. For each subset the sum of its elements, the product of its elements and the sum of the digits of all its elements are calculated. Is it possible that $A$ alone has the largest sum of elements, $B$ alone has the largest product of elements, and $C$ alone has the largest sum of digits?

bw.2016.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.7.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which $$3x^n+n(x+2)-3\geq nx^2$$ holds for all real numbers $x$.

bw.2016.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.8.reviewed_statement:
Find all real numbers $a$ for which there exists a non-constant function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying the following two equations for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$:
(i) $f(ax)=a^2f(x)$ and
(ii) $f\big(f(x)\big)=af(x)$.

bw.2016.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.9.reviewed_statement: Find all quadruples $(a,b,c,d)$ of real numbers that simultaneously satisfy the following equations: $$\begin{cases}a^3+c^3=2\\ a^2b+c^2d=0\\ b^3+d^3=1\\ ab^2+cd^2=-6.\end{cases}$$

bw.2016.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.10.reviewed_statement: Let $a_{0,1}, a_{0,2}, \ldots, a_{0,2016}$ be positive real numbers. For $n\geq 0$ and $1\leq k<2016$ set $$a_{n+1,k}=a_{n,k}+\frac{1}{2a_{n,k+1}}\quad\text{and}\quad a_{n+1,2016}=a_{n,2016}+\frac{1}{2a_{n,1}}.$$ Show that $\max_{1\leq k\leq 2016}a_{2016,k}>44$.

bw.2016.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.11.reviewed_statement: Set $A$ consists of $2016$ positive integers. All prime divisors of these numbers are smaller than $30$. Prove that there are four distinct numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ in $A$ such that $abcd$ is a perfect square.

bw.2016.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.12.reviewed_statement: Does there exist a hexagon (not necessarily convex) with side lengths $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ (not necessarily in this order) that can be tiled with (a) $31$, (b) $32$ equilateral triangles with side length $1$?

bw.2016.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ numbers all equal to $1$ be written on a blackboard. A move consists of replacing two numbers on the board with two copies of their sum. It happens that after $h$ moves all $n$ numbers on the blackboard are equal to $m$. Prove that $h\leq\frac12n\log_2 m$.

bw.2016.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.14.reviewed_statement: A cube consists of $4^3$ unit cubes each containing an integer. At each move, you choose a unit cube and increase by $1$ all the integers in the neighbouring cubes having a face in common with the chosen cube. Is it possible to reach a position where all the $4^3$ integers are divisible by $3$, no matter what the starting position is?

bw.2016.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.15.reviewed_statement: The Baltic Sea has $2016$ harbours. There are two-way ferry connections between some of them. It is impossible to make a sequence of direct voyages $C_1-C_2-\cdots-C_{1062}$ where all the harbours $C_1, \ldots, C_{1062}$ are distinct. Prove that there exist two disjoint sets $A$ and $B$ of $477$ harbours each, such that there is no harbour in $A$ with a direct ferry connection to a harbour in $B$.

bw.2016.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.16.reviewed_statement: In triangle $ABC$, the points $D$ and $E$ are the intersections of the angular bisectors from $C$ and $B$ with the sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Points $F$ and $G$ on the extensions of $AB$ and $AC$ beyond $B$ and $C$, respectively, satisfy $BF=CG=BC$. Prove that $FG\parallel DE$.

bw.2016.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB=AD$. Let $T$ be a point on the diagonal $AC$ such that $\angle ABT+\angle ADT=\angle BCD$. Prove that $AT+AC\geq AB+AD$.

bw.2016.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram such that $\angle BAD=60^\circ$. Let $K$ and $L$ be the midpoints of $BC$ and $CD$, respectively. Assuming that $ABKL$ is a cyclic quadrilateral, find $\angle ABD$.

bw.2016.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.19.reviewed_statement: Consider triangles in the plane where each vertex has integer coordinates. Such a triangle can be legally transformed by moving one vertex parallel to the opposite side to a different point with integer coordinates. Show that if two triangles have the same area, then there exists a series of legal transformations that transforms one to the other.

bw.2016.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2016.0.20.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $AB$ and $CD$ not parallel. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CD$. Let $P$ be a point inside $ABCD$ such that $PA=PB=CM$. Prove that $AB$, $CD$ and the perpendicular bisector of $MP$ are concurrent.

bw.2017.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots$ be an infinite sequence of real numbers satisfying $\frac{a_{n-1}+a_{n+1}}{2}\geq a_n$ for all positive integers $n$. Show that $$\frac{a_0+a_{n+1}}{2}\geq\frac{a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n}{n}$$ holds for all positive integers $n$.

bw.2017.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.2.reviewed_statement: Does there exist a finite set of real numbers such that their sum equals $2$, the sum of their squares equals $3$, the sum of their cubes equals $4$, $\ldots$, and the sum of their ninth powers equals $10$?

bw.2017.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.3.reviewed_statement:
Positive integers $x_1, \ldots, x_m$ (not necessarily distinct) are written on a blackboard. It is known that each of the numbers $F_1, \ldots, F_{2018}$ can be represented as a sum of one or more of the numbers on the blackboard. What is the smallest possible value of $m$?
(Here $F_1, \ldots, F_{2018}$ are the first $2018$ Fibonacci numbers: $F_1=F_2=1$, $F_{k+1}=F_k+F_{k-1}$ for $k>1$.)

bw.2017.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.4.reviewed_statement: A linear form in $k$ variables is an expression of the form $P(x_1, \ldots, x_k)=a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k$ with real constants $a_1, \ldots, a_k$. Prove that there exist a positive integer $n$ and linear forms $P_1, \ldots, P_n$ in $2017$ variables such that the equation $$x_1\cdot x_2\cdots x_{2017}=P_1(x_1, \ldots, x_{2017})^{2017}+\cdots+P_n(x_1, \ldots, x_{2017})^{2017}$$ holds for all real numbers $x_1, \ldots, x_{2017}$.

bw.2017.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(x^2y)=f(xy)+yf\big(f(x)+y\big)$$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

bw.2017.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.6.reviewed_statement:
Fifteen stones are placed on a $4\times 4$ board, one in each cell, the remaining cell being empty. Whenever two stones are on neighbouring cells (having a common side), one may jump over the other to the opposite neighbouring cell, provided this cell is empty. The stone jumped over is removed from the board.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2017_p6_fig.png

For which initial positions of the empty cell is it possible to end up with exactly one stone on the board?

bw.2017.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.7.reviewed_statement:
Each edge of a complete graph on $30$ vertices is coloured either red or blue. It is allowed to choose a non-monochromatic triangle and change the colour of the two edges of the same colour to make the triangle monochromatic. Prove that by using this operation repeatedly it is possible to make the entire graph monochromatic.
(A complete graph is a graph where any two vertices are connected by an edge.)

bw.2017.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.8.reviewed_statement:
A chess knight has injured his leg and is limping. He alternates between a normal move and a short move where he moves to any diagonally neighbouring cell.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2017_p8_fig.png

The limping knight moves on a $5\times 6$ cell chessboard starting with a normal move. What is the largest number of moves he can make if he is starting from a cell of his own choice and is not allowed to visit any cell (including the initial cell) more than once?

bw.2017.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.9.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $n$ is Danish if a regular hexagon can be partitioned into $n$ congruent polygons. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that both $n$ and $2^n+n$ are Danish.

bw.2017.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.10.reviewed_statement: Maker and Breaker are building a wall. Maker has a supply of green cubical building blocks, and Breaker has a supply of red ones, all of the same size. On the ground, a row of $m$ squares has been marked in chalk as place-holders. Maker and Breaker now take turns in placing a block either directly on one of these squares, or on top of another block already in place, in such a way that the height of each column never exceeds $n$. Maker places the first block. Maker bets that he can form a green row, i.e. all $m$ blocks at a certain height are green. Breaker bets that he can prevent Maker from achieving this. Determine all pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers for which Maker can make sure he wins the bet.

bw.2017.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $H$ and $I$ be the orthocentre and incentre, respectively, of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. The circumcircle of the triangle $BCI$ intersects the segment $AB$ at the point $P$ different from $B$. Let $K$ be the projection of $H$ onto $AI$ and $Q$ the reflection of $P$ in $K$. Show that $B$, $H$ and $Q$ are collinear.

bw.2017.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.12.reviewed_statement: Line $\ell$ touches circle $S_1$ in the point $X$ and circle $S_2$ in the point $Y$. We draw a line $m$ which is parallel to $\ell$ and intersects $S_1$ in a point $P$ and $S_2$ in a point $Q$. Prove that the ratio $XP/YQ$ does not depend on the choice of $m$.

bw.2017.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle in which $\angle ABC=60^\circ$. Let $I$ and $O$ be the incentre and circumcentre of $ABC$, respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$, which does not contain the point $A$. Determine $\angle BAC$ given that $MB=OI$.

bw.2017.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.14.reviewed_statement: Let $P$ be a point inside the acute angle $BAC$. Suppose that $\angle ABP=\angle ACP=90^\circ$. The points $D$ and $E$ are on the segments $BA$ and $CA$, respectively, such that $BD=BP$ and $CP=CE$. The points $F$ and $G$ are on the segments $AC$ and $AB$, respectively, such that $DF$ is perpendicular to $AB$ and $EG$ is perpendicular to $AC$. Show that $PF=PG$.

bw.2017.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.15.reviewed_statement: Let $n\geq 3$ be an integer. What is the largest possible number of interior angles greater than $180^\circ$ in an $n$-gon in the plane, given that the $n$-gon does not intersect itself and all its sides have the same length?

bw.2017.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.16.reviewed_statement: Is it possible for any group of people to choose a positive integer $N$ and assign a positive integer to each person in the group such that the product of two persons' numbers is divisible by $N$ if and only if they are friends?

bw.2017.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.17.reviewed_statement: Determine whether the equation $$x^4+y^3=z!+7$$ has an infinite number of solutions in positive integers.

bw.2017.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $p>3$ be a prime and let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{\frac{p-1}{2}}$ be a permutation of $1, 2, \ldots, \frac{p-1}{2}$. For which $p$ is it always possible to determine the sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{\frac{p-1}{2}}$ if for all $i,j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, \frac{p-1}{2}\}$ with $i\neq j$ the residue of $a_ia_j$ modulo $p$ is known?

bw.2017.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.19.reviewed_statement:
For an integer $n\geq 1$ let $a(n)$ denote the total number of carries which arise when adding $2017$ and $n\cdot 2017$. The first few values are given by $a(1)=1$, $a(2)=1$, $a(3)=0$, which can be seen from the following (the first row shows the carries):
$$\begin{array}{rcrcr} 001 & \qquad & 001 & \qquad & 000\\ 2017 & & 4034 & & 6051\\ +2017 & & +2017 & & +2017\\ =4034 & & =6051 & & =8068\end{array}$$
Prove that $$a(1)+a(2)+\cdots+a(10^{2017}-1)=10\cdot\frac{10^{2017}-1}{9}.$$

bw.2017.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2017.0.20.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be the set of all ordered pairs $(a,b)$ of integers with $0<2a<2b<2017$ such that $a^2+b^2$ is a multiple of $2017$. Prove that $$\sum_{(a,b)\in S}a=\frac12\sum_{(a,b)\in S}b.$$

bw.2018.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.1.reviewed_statement: A finite collection of positive real numbers (not necessarily distinct) is balanced if each number is less than the sum of the others. Find all $m\geq 3$ such that every balanced finite collection of $m$ numbers can be split into three parts with the property that the sum of the numbers in each part is less than the sum of the numbers in the two other parts.

bw.2018.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.2.reviewed_statement: A $100\times 100$ table is given. For each $k$, $1\leq k\leq 100$, the $k$-th row of the table contains the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, k$ in increasing order (from left to right) but not necessarily in consecutive cells; the remaining $100-k$ cells are filled with zeroes. Prove that there exist two columns such that the sum of the numbers in one of the columns is at least $19$ times as large as the sum of the numbers in the other column.

bw.2018.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be positive real numbers such that $abcd=1$. Prove the inequality $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{a+2b+3c+10}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{b+2c+3d+10}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{c+2d+3a+10}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d+2a+3b+10}}\leq 1.$$

bw.2018.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.4.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ such that for any positive integer $n$ and for any non-negative real numbers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ $$f(x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2)=f(x_1)^2+\cdots+f(x_n)^2.$$

bw.2018.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.5.reviewed_statement: A polynomial $f(x)$ with real coefficients is called generating if for each polynomial $\varphi(x)$ with real coefficients there exist a positive integer $k$ and polynomials $g_1(x), \ldots, g_k(x)$ with real coefficients such that $$\varphi(x)=f\big(g_1(x)\big)+\cdots+f\big(g_k(x)\big).$$ Find all generating polynomials.

bw.2018.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.6.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Elfie the Elf travels in $\mathbb{R}^3$. She starts at the origin $(0,0,0)$. In each turn she can teleport to any point with integer coordinates which lies at distance exactly $\sqrt{n}$ from her current location. However, teleportation is a complicated procedure: Elfie starts off normal but she turns strange with her first teleportation. Next time she teleports she turns normal again, then strange again, etc. For which $n$ can Elfie travel to any point with integer coordinates and be normal when she gets there?

bw.2018.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.7.reviewed_statement:
On a $16\times 16$ torus as shown all $512$ edges are colored red or blue. A coloring is good if every vertex is an endpoint of an even number of red edges. A move consists of switching the color of each of the $4$ edges of an arbitrary cell. What is the largest number of good colorings such that none of them can be converted to another by a sequence of moves?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2018_p7_fig.png

bw.2018.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.8.reviewed_statement: A graph has $N$ vertices. An invisible hare sits in one of the vertices. A group of hunters tries to kill the hare. In each move all of them shoot simultaneously: each hunter shoots at a single vertex, they choose the target vertices cooperatively. If the hare was in one of the target vertices during a shoot, the hunt is finished. Otherwise the hare can stay in its vertex or jump to one of the neighbouring vertices. The hunters know an algorithm that allows them to kill the hare in at most $N!$ moves. Prove that then there exists an algorithm that allows them to kill the hare in at most $2^N$ moves.

bw.2018.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.9.reviewed_statement:
Olga and Sasha play a game on an infinite hexagonal grid. They take turns in placing a stone on a free hexagon of their choice. Olga starts the game. Just before the $2018$th stone is placed, a new rule comes into play. A stone may now be placed only on those free hexagons having at least two occupied neighbors. A player loses when she or he either is unable to make a move, or makes a move such that a pattern of the rhomboid shape as shown (rotated in any possible way) appears. Determine which player, if any, possesses a winning strategy.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2018_p9_fig.png

bw.2018.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.10.reviewed_statement: The integers from $1$ to $n$ are written, one on each of $n$ cards. The first player removes one card. Then the second player removes two cards with consecutive integers. After that the first player removes three cards with consecutive integers. Finally, the second player removes four cards with consecutive integers. What is the smallest value of $n$ for which the second player can ensure that he completes both his moves?

bw.2018.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.11.reviewed_statement: The points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ lie, in this order, on a circle $\omega$, where $AD$ is a diameter of $\omega$. Furthermore, $AB=BC=a$ and $CD=c$ for some relatively prime integers $a$ and $c$. Show that if the diameter $d$ of $\omega$ is also an integer, then either $d$ or $2d$ is a perfect square.

bw.2018.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.12.reviewed_statement: The altitudes $BB_1$ and $CC_1$ of an acute triangle $ABC$ intersect in point $H$. Let $B_2$ and $C_2$ be points on the segments $BH$ and $CH$, respectively, such that $BB_2=B_1H$ and $CC_2=C_1H$. The circumcircle of the triangle $B_2HC_2$ intersects the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ in points $D$ and $E$. Prove that the triangle $DEH$ is right-angled.

bw.2018.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.13.reviewed_statement: The bisector of the angle $A$ of a triangle $ABC$ intersects $BC$ in a point $D$ and intersects the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ in a point $E$. Let $K$, $L$, $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the segments $AB$, $BD$, $CD$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $P$ be the circumcentre of the triangle $EKL$, and $Q$ be the circumcentre of the triangle $EMN$. Prove that $\angle PEQ=\angle BAC$.

bw.2018.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.14.reviewed_statement: A quadrilateral $ABCD$ is circumscribed about a circle $\omega$. The intersection point of $\omega$ and the diagonal $AC$, closest to $A$, is $E$. The point $F$ is diametrically opposite to the point $E$ on the circle $\omega$. The tangent to $\omega$ at the point $F$ intersects lines $AB$ and $BC$ in points $A_1$ and $C_1$, and lines $AD$ and $CD$ in points $A_2$ and $C_2$, respectively. Prove that $A_1C_1=A_2C_2$.

bw.2018.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.15.reviewed_statement: Two circles in the plane do not intersect and do not lie inside each other. We choose diameters $A_1B_1$ and $A_2B_2$ of these circles such that the segments $A_1A_2$ and $B_1B_2$ intersect. Let $A$ and $B$ be the midpoints of the segments $A_1A_2$ and $B_1B_2$, and $C$ be the intersection point of these segments. Prove that the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$ belongs to a fixed line that does not depend on the choice of diameters.

bw.2018.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Find all positive integers $n$ for which $\sqrt{n^2-np}$ is a positive integer.

bw.2018.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.17.reviewed_statement: Prove that for any positive integers $p$, $q$ such that $\sqrt{11}>\frac{p}{q}$, the following inequality holds: $$\sqrt{11}-\frac{p}{q}>\frac{1}{2pq}.$$

bw.2018.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $n\geq 3$ be an integer such that $4n+1$ is a prime number. Prove that $4n+1$ divides $n^{2n}-1$.

bw.2018.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.19.reviewed_statement: An infinite set $B$ consisting of positive integers has the following property: for each $a,b\in B$ with $a>b$ the number $\frac{a-b}{(a,b)}$ belongs to $B$. Prove that $B$ contains all positive integers. Here, $(a,b)$ is the greatest common divisor of numbers $a$ and $b$.

bw.2018.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2018.0.20.reviewed_statement: Find all the triples of positive integers $(a,b,c)$ for which the number $$\frac{(a+b)^4}{c}+\frac{(b+c)^4}{a}+\frac{(c+a)^4}{b}$$ is an integer and $a+b+c$ is a prime.

bw.2019.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.1.reviewed_statement: For all non-negative real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ with $x\geq y$, prove the inequality $$\frac{x^3-y^3+z^3+1}{6}\geq(x-y)\sqrt{xyz}.$$

bw.2019.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $(F_n)$ be the sequence defined recursively by $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1}$ for $n\geq 2$. Find all pairs of positive integers $(x,y)$ such that $$5F_x-3F_y=1.$$

bw.2019.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.3.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f\big(xf(y)-y^2\big)=(y+1)f(x-y)$$ holds for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

bw.2019.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.4.reviewed_statement: Determine all integers $n$ for which there exist an integer $k\geq 2$ and positive integers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k$ so that $$x_1x_2+x_2x_3+\cdots+x_{k-1}x_k=n\quad\text{and}\quad x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_k=2019.$$

bw.2019.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.5.reviewed_statement: The $2m$ numbers $$1\cdot 2,\ 2\cdot 3,\ 3\cdot 4,\ \ldots,\ 2m(2m+1)$$ are written on a blackboard, where $m\geq 2$ is an integer. A move consists of choosing three numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, erasing them from the board and writing the single number $$\frac{abc}{ab+bc+ca}.$$ After $m-1$ such moves, only two numbers will remain on the blackboard. Supposing one of these is $\frac43$, show that the other is larger than $4$.

bw.2019.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.6.reviewed_statement: Alice and Bob play the following game. They write the expressions $x+y$, $x-y$, $x^2+xy+y^2$ and $x^2-xy+y^2$ each on a separate card. The four cards are shuffled and placed face down on a table. One of the cards is turned over, revealing the expression written on it, after which Alice chooses any two of the four cards, and gives the other two to Bob. All cards are then revealed. Now Alice picks one of the variables $x$ and $y$, assigns a real value to it, and tells Bob what value she assigned and to which variable. Then Bob assigns a real value to the other variable. Finally, they both evaluate the product of the expressions on their two cards. Whoever gets the larger result wins. Which player, if any, has a winning strategy?

bw.2019.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.7.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest integer $k\geq 2$ such that for every partition of the set $\{2, 3, \ldots, k\}$ into two parts, at least one of these parts contains (not necessarily distinct) numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ with $ab=c$.

bw.2019.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.8.reviewed_statement: There are $2019$ cities in the country of Balticwayland. Some pairs of cities are connected by non-intersecting bidirectional roads, each road connecting exactly $2$ cities. It is known that for every pair of cities $A$ and $B$ it is possible to drive from $A$ to $B$ using at most $2$ roads. There are $62$ cops trying to catch a robber. The cops and robber all know each others' locations at all times. Each night, the robber can choose to stay in her current city or move to a neighbouring city via a direct road. Each day, each cop has the same choice of staying or moving, and they coordinate their actions. The robber is caught if she is in the same city as a cop at any time. Prove that the cops can always catch the robber.

bw.2019.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.9.reviewed_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, consider all nonincreasing functions $f:\{1, \ldots, n\}\to\{1, \ldots, n\}$. Some of them have a fixed point (i.e. a $c$ such that $f(c)=c$), some do not. Determine the difference between the sizes of the two sets of functions.
Remark: A function $f$ is nonincreasing if $f(x)\geq f(y)$ holds for all $x\leq y$.

bw.2019.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.10.reviewed_statement: There are $2019$ points given in the plane. A child wants to draw $k$ (closed) discs in such a manner that for any two distinct points there exists a disc that contains exactly one of these two points. What is the minimal $k$ such that for any initial configuration of points it is possible to draw $k$ discs with the above property?

bw.2019.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let the circles with diameters $AC$ and $BM$ intersect at points $M$ and $P$. Let $MP$ intersect $AB$ at $Q$. Let $R$ be a point on $AP$ such that $QR\parallel BP$. Prove that $CP$ bisects $\angle RCB$.

bw.2019.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $H$ its orthocentre. Let $D$ be a point lying on the segment $AC$ and let $E$ be the point on the line $BC$ such that $BC\perp DE$. Prove that $EH\perp BD$ if and only if $BD$ bisects $AE$.

bw.2019.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon in which $AB=AF$, $BC=CD$, $DE=EF$ and $\angle ABC=\angle EFA=90^\circ$. Prove that $AD\perp CE$.

bw.2019.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.14.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, and let $H$ be the foot of the altitude from $B$. The points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of the segments $AH$ and $CH$, respectively. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the second points of intersection of the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ with the lines $BM$ and $BN$, respectively. The segments $AQ$ and $CP$ intersect at the point $R$. Prove that the line $BR$ passes through the midpoint of the segment $MN$.

bw.2019.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.15.reviewed_statement:
Let $n\geq 4$, and consider a (not necessarily convex) polygon $P_1P_2\cdots P_n$ in the plane. Suppose that, for each $P_k$, there is a unique vertex $Q_k\neq P_k$ among $P_1, \ldots, P_n$ that lies closest to it. The polygon is then said to be hostile if $Q_k\neq P_{k\pm 1}$ for all $k$ (where $P_0=P_n$, $P_{n+1}=P_1$).
(a) Prove that no hostile polygon is convex.
(b) Find all $n\geq 4$ for which there exists a hostile $n$-gon.

bw.2019.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.16.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $N$, let $f(N)$ be the number of ordered pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ such that the number $$\frac{ab}{a+b}$$ is a divisor of $N$. Prove that $f(N)$ is always a perfect square.

bw.2019.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Show that for every integer $c$, there exists an integer $a$ such that $$a^{\frac{p+1}{2}}+(a+c)^{\frac{p+1}{2}}\equiv c\pmod p.$$

bw.2019.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2019.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be odd positive integers such that $a$ is not a perfect square and $$a^2+a+1=3(b^2+b+1)(c^2+c+1).$$ Prove that at least one of the numbers $b^2+b+1$ and $c^2+c+1$ is composite.
